findings.title: Overwrite-guard tasks do not cover the `sq review code` path named in the success criterion
findings.description: T12/T13 add and test the fail-closed archive guard only in `review/persistence.save_review_file`. The success criterion "Re-running `sq review code <N>` over an edited review file archives the prior content and warns; nothing is silently destroyed" cannot be met by that scope: `src/squadron/cli/commands/review.py:746` calls `save_review_result`, which writes directly via `path.write_text(...)` with no archive attempt and no guard; `save_review_file` is reached only from the pipeline action's fallback path (`src/squadron/pipeline/actions/review.py:272`). File 1's own T10 already identifies `save_review_result` as the CLI persistence path for Part A, so Part D's scoping is internally inconsistent. Add a task that applies the same guard to `save_review_result` (or routes the CLI through the guarded function) and extend T13 to test the `sq review code`/`save_review_result` path.

findings.title: T14 verification checkpoint is numbered after the Part D work it gates
findings.description: The design's Phase 5 note requires the cf archive-scanning verification to be "sequenced before Part D lands — it is a go/no-go on the archive filename scheme." T14 is placed after T12/T13 and relies on a prose note ("do not mark T12 done until T14 is known") to reverse the order. A junior working the checklist top-down will implement the archive scheme before the go/no-go that may force mangling it. Move T14 ahead of T12 (and renumber) so the dependency is expressed by task order rather than by a caveat.

findings.title: Unreadable-judge-response failure mode has no test on the resolve path
findings.description: The success criterion requires that "Judge transport failure and an unreadable judge response on the resolve path yield UNKNOWN with a WARNING." T26 tests a transport raise (`judge transport mocked to raise`) and the cap, but never an unreadable/unparseable judge response. `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/findings_addressed/judge.py` has two distinct fail-closed branches — the `except Exception` transport branch and the `is_parse_failure(residue, statuses)` branch — and only the first is exercised; T6's unchanged 305 suite covers parse failure on the pipeline path, not this path. Add a case where the mocked judge returns output with no readable status lines and assert UNKNOWN plus a WARNING.

findings.title: Injection-cap step leaves the threshold and measurement undefined
findings.description: T25 says to "reuse whatever threshold/measurement 305's architecture already defines for the injection cap," and T26 requires a diff "constructed to exceed the injection cap." I found no diff-injection cap in `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/findings_addressed/`; the only configured caps are `review.max_file_size_bytes` and `review.max_total_injection_bytes` in `src/squadron/config/keys.py`, applied to file injection in `review/review_client.py`, not to a diff string passed in as `inputs`. A junior has no concrete value or measurement to implement or test against. Name the cap source and measurement explicitly in T25 and the over-cap fixture in T26.

findings.title: "Review discovery" from the metrology criterion is not exercised by T32
findings.description: The success criterion asks that both `discover_judge_results` *and review discovery* return no resolution artifacts, tested against the real glob. T32 tests only `discover_judge_results`; the precedent `tests/metrology/test_capture_discovery.py` also covers only that function. The other review-discovery surface is `resolve_target` in `src/squadron/metrology/capture.py`, which globs `{index}-review.*`. Add a `resolve_target` assertion to T32. The behavior is likely correct by construction (the `-resolution.` filename contains no `-review.`), but that is exactly what the criterion asks to demonstrate rather than infer.

findings.title: Part 0 verification repeats the same suite three times
findings.description: Eight tasks cover a move the design calls mechanical. T2 runs the five-file 305 suite plus pyright; T4 runs the identical command again; T6 re-runs a subset; T8 then runs the full suite, ruff, and pyright. Merge the models/parsing/verification moves (T1 + T3) into one move task with one verify, keep T5/T6 for the judge extraction and T7/T8 for exports plus final suite. That removes two redundant verification tasks without weakening the "305 suite unchanged" criterion.

findings.title: Most success criteria trace cleanly to implementation/test pairs
findings.description: The `reviewedSha` stamp and git-unavailable omission (T9–T11), empty-diff and git-failure screens (T21/T22), `--no-judge` (T25/T26), untouched-path `verify_outcomes` downgrade (T27/T28), file-history fallback and `--since` precedence (T19/T20), verdict-consistency screen (T23/T24), archive-copy verification with fail-closed abort (T12/T13), unchanged 305 suite after relocation (T2/T4/T6/T8), and `-r2` versioning (T31/T32) each have a corresponding task and an immediately following test task. Commit markers are plain non-checkbox lines placed after tested points, and no scope-creep task was found.
